subject: Granary Health renewal — pricing, credits, and 90-day price-hold request
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@granaryhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@granaryhealth.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal pricing and timing

Hi Kimberly,

We’re starting procurement for our platform renewals and wanted to check in on Granary’s renewal with Redwood. We’re very happy with performance but our procurement team needs a firm pricing path and a short-term price-hold while we finalize PO timing.

Two quick asks:
- Can Redwood hold existing rates for 60–90 days while procurement completes their review?
- Given our steady growth, can you outline options for a small capacity uplift (20% burst or temporary dedicated nodes) and any associated credits or discounts?

Attached is our Q2 usage report for reference. Our procurement deadline is the week of Sep 6; if we can get a term sheet and pricing by Sep 2 that would help accelerate approval.

Thanks — happy to set a quick call if easier.

Best,
Sarah Kim
Head of Cloud Ops
Granary Health

Attachment: Granary_Usage_Q2.pdf (summary)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@granaryhealth.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing and timing

Hi Sarah — thanks for the note and the usage file.

Short answer: yes, we can propose a 60–90 day price-hold depending on term and commit, and we can structure a temporary capacity uplift with conditional credits. I’ve looped in Dylan (account lead) and Vivek (solutions) to run numbers and surface options.

Plan:
- Dylan will pull the last 12 months of token/embedding consumption and model mix to scope uplift cost.
- I’ll draft two term-sheet options: (A) 12-month renewal with 60-day price-hold + conditional credits for true-ups, and (B) 24-month renewal with 90-day price-hold and deeper discounts if Granary converts a portion of usage to a committed tier.

Dylan — can you run a baseline projection and a 20% burst scenario? Vivek, flag anything on the infra side for dedicated nodes.

Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
Direct: (415) 555-0198

Attachment: Placeholder - will attach term sheet draft in follow up.

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@granaryhealth.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing and timing

Kimberly / Sarah — pulled the numbers this morning. Summary below (high level):

Baseline (last 3 months, normalized): 1.2B tokens/month, ~18M embedding units/month. Model mix: 65% open-encoder variants / 35% larger gen models.

Projected 20% uplift (burst window): 1.44B tokens/month average during peak weeks. Expected incremental cost if fully pay-as-you-go: ~$62k/month.

Options I recommend we include in the term sheet:
- Option A: 12m term, maintain current headline rate for 60 days (price-hold), committed minimum = current avg monthly * 12, with a 10% staged credit applied to overages in months 1–3 after uplift.
- Option B: 24m term, 90-day price-hold, commit to 20% uplift capacity as part of the commit (blended rate), plus an upfront credit equal to 5% of first-year invoice applied over quarters as usage rebate.
- Temporary dedicated nodes (optional): 2x T4-equivalent nodes for burst windows with a fixed monthly add-on and a one-off onboarding fee. We can make the nodes ephemeral for 3 months and then convert to reserved if desired.

I’ll attach a spreadsheet with month-by-month spend scenarios. If Granary’s procurement needs a line item for "price-hold", we should call it out as a conditional clause tied to receipt of signed term sheet + PO within the hold window.

-Dylan
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Granary_Spend_Scenarios_Q2-Q4.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@granaryhealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@granaryhealth.com
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing and timing

Thanks Dylan — this is helpful. Procurement confirms they need a formal term sheet with the price-hold clause wording and an explicit PO cut-off date. A couple clarifications:

1) The procurement team will only accept a price-hold if the term sheet specifies the hold duration and the exact trigger for when it ends (e.g., PO signed by Sep 15 or automatic expiration).
2) For the dedicated nodes: procurement prefers capped monthly billing rather than a usage variable line item. Can you provide a capped cost option we can include?

Can you include the above in the term sheet and send by Sep 6? That gives procurement time to review before the Sep 15 internal deadline. Happy to hop on a 30m call if helpful.

Best —
Sarah
Head of Cloud Ops, Granary Health

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Granary Health — draft term sheet and pricing offer (v3)

Sarah / Procurement team — thanks for the quick responses. Attached is an updated term sheet (Granary_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf) and a short one-page summary. Key points summarized here for quick review: 

Offer summary (consolidated):
- Price-hold: 90-day price-hold from execution of this term sheet, conditional on receiving a PO within that window. If PO received within 90 days, current rates will apply for the first 12 months.
- Commit structure (two tracks):
  • Track 1 (12m): Commit = current 12-month baseline. 60-day hold. Overages subject to 10% staged credit for months 1–3 after uplift.
  • Track 2 (24m): Commit = baseline + 20% uplift blended into the commit. 90-day hold. Upfront 5% first-year credit applied quarterly.
- Dedicated nodes: We can offer a capped dedicated burst option: fixed monthly fee of $28k/month for up to 2x nodes during the 3-month burst window (no per-token billing during that capped period). Onboarding fee: $3,500 (one-time).
- Credits & invoicing: Credits will be applied as invoice line items and visible in the Redwood Console. We’ll provide month-by-month scenarios to attach to the PO.
- Next steps: If Granary prefers Track 2, we’ll produce an amendment for a 24-month SLA-backed commit and draft the DocuSign for execution. If Track 1, we’ll keep the shorter hold and staged credit.

Requested actions:
1) Procurement: confirm which track you prefer and whether the capped dedicated node fee is acceptable as a line item.
2) Sarah: confirm if you want us to route the DocuSign to procurement directly or to you first for review.

We’ve included the language for the price-hold clause directly in the attached term sheet under Section 2. Let me know if you want redlines; we can turn this around same day.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
